title: Critical fix flow, branching matrix, and fast recovery triage
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and stabilize a repeatable emergency fix and rollback process that codifies severity criteria, branch lifecycle, backport timelines, and staged rollout gates for LTS and mainline channels. This ticket captures decisions, examples, and a concise playbook for on-call and release engineers.
background: We currently have ad-hoc hotpatch workflows that vary by team. That variability increases time-to-restore and causes duplicate backport work. We need one canonical flow that: 1) maps severity to branches and SLAs, 2) prescribes safe patch branching and cherry-picking rules, 3) defines rollout gates and metrics for automatic rollback, and 4) documents a short, checklist-style runbook for on-call.
severity_criteria:
Severity levels and target time-to-fix (TTF):
- Severity: Critical (S0) — production outage causing major feature loss or data corruption. Target: 0-4 hours to mitigation, 24 hours to stable patch. Customer impact: high.
- Severity: High (S1) — degraded performance or incorrect outputs impacting a significant subset of customers. Target: 4-12 hours to mitigation, 72 hours to patch. Customer impact: medium-high.
- Severity: Medium (S2) — functional regressions with workarounds. Target: 72 hours to patch. Customer impact: medium.
- Severity: Low (S3) — cosmetic or minor behavioral issues. Target: next minor release. Customer impact: low.
branching_strategy:
Branching model guidance:
- main: active development (non-LTS). All feature merges land here.
- release/X.Y: short-lived release branches for upcoming point releases.
- lts/X.Y: long-term support branches (only security and critical bug fixes).
- patch/ENG-<id>/X.Y.Z: ephemeral branches created for urgent patches. Naming convention enforces traceability.
Commands (examples):
- Create a patch branch from target branch: git checkout -b patch/ENG-94533/release-1.22.3 origin/release/1.22
- After validation, cherry-pick to LTS or main as required: git cherry-pick <commit> && git push origin patch/ENG-94533/release-1.22.3
- Merge back with signed commits and required approvals using hotfix PR template.
Notes: Never directly commit to lts/* or release/* without a PR and two approvers (one from release engineering).
patch_branch_naming:
Conventions for patch branches (required):
- patch/ENG-<ticket>-<target> e.g., patch/ENG-94533/release-1.22
- Include ticket key and target branch to make CI traceability trivial.
- Add suffix /wip for early experimental fixes, remove before PR to signal readiness.
backport_matrix:
Backport rules by severity and target channels: 
- S0 (Critical): Apply to all active channels (main, release/X.Y, lts/X.Y) within 24 hours. Backports required for the last two LTS majors.
- S1 (High): Backport to release/X.Y and latest LTS branch within 72 hours; main if fix intersects ongoing development.
- S2 (Medium): Accept for release channels on cadence; LTS only if regression affects customers and no workaround.
- S3 (Low): No immediate backport; include in next scheduled patch cycle.
Backport ownership: original author + release engineer on rotation. Use the backport checklist included in the PR template.
gating_and_rollout:
Rollout gates and observability thresholds:
- Canary stages: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over configurable windows (default 15m per stage).
- Gate metrics (trigger an automatic rollback if threshold breached within stage window):
  - Error rate increase > 3x baseline OR absolute error rate > 0.5%
  - Latency P95 increase > 200ms over baseline
  - Model regression metrics (for inference): quality drop > 2% on canary prompt set or new hallucination signals detected
- Manual approval required before promoting from 25% -> 100% for S0 fixes.
- Rollback policy: prefer feature-flag-based disable when available; otherwise execute rollback PR to revert the merge and activate patch-channel mitigation.
playbook_steps:
Concise emergency runbook for on-call and release engineers: 
1) Triage & severity decision (owner: on-call): confirm S0/S1 and notify stakeholders via incident channel.
2) Create ticket and patch branch: use patch/ENG-<id>/target naming.
3) Implement minimal fix + unit and regression tests.
4) Open hotfix PR with backport checklist, link incident docs, and assign two approvers (release eng + code owner).
5) Run dedicated hotpatch CI pipeline (fast test subset + canary deploy).
6) Canary deploy and monitor gate metrics for 30 minutes. If green, progress to wider rollout per gating policy.
7) If gate fails, trigger rollback documented in the PR and call a postmortem if S0.
8) After merge, cherry-pick commits to required branches, tag patch releases, and communicate release notes and migration guidance.
Quick commands: git checkout -b patch/ENG-94533/release-1.22; git commit -s -m "ENG-94533: fix shard allocation crash"; hub pull-request -b release/1.22 -m "hotfix: ENG-94533 - shard allocation crash".
pr_and_review_guidelines:
PR template and requirements for hotfix PRs:
- Title prefix: hotfix: ENG-<id> - short summary
- Checklist fields: Severity declared, Test coverage added, Canary plan, Backport targets listed, Release engineer assigned, Security sign-off if data-sensitive.
- Required approvals: release-eng lead or duty engineer + code owner.
- Labeling: hotfix, emergency, backport-required (as applicable).
post_release_tasks:
Post-release stabilization and follow-ups:
- Run a targeted smoke test runbook and validate telemetry for 24-72 hours.
- Create postmortem for S0 incidents and link to this ticket.
- Update the backport ledger (internal doc) with branches updated and commits cherry-picked.
- Schedule a retro in the release-infra weekly sync if process deviations occurred.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical hotfix PR template exists in the repo and is linked from this ticket
CI pipeline for hotpatch runs a fast, deterministic test subset and can trigger canary deploys
Automated canary rollback thresholds are implemented in staging and tested
Documentation (this ticket -> Confluence runbook) is published and referenced in on-call playbooks
